name: Southwest Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Lower-angle alpine rock gaining the ridge crest
Below the crux; rack up for the final pitch here
Runout final pitch to the summit; climbing slightly climber's-right of the described line reported as easier

descent_text: From the summit, descend via the West Ridge's 3rd-4th class scramble and snow/ice gully back onto the Terror Glacier (rather than rappelling the southwest ridge), then re-cross the glacier and slabs to the lake outlet and climb back out over the 6,200' notch to the Goodell Creek trail.
approach: Identical to the West Ridge approach: Goodell Creek trailhead to Terror Basin over the 6,200' notch, then traverse benches/slabs to the glacial lake outlet and up slabs onto the Terror Glacier. From there, continue to the east end of the Terror Glacier to reach the base of the southwest ridge (rather than the west-ridge gully used by the standard route).
overview: A sustained six-pitch 5.8- alpine rock line up West McMillan Spire's southwest ridge, harder and more technical than the standard West Ridge scramble but sharing the same long approach via Terror Basin and the Terror Glacier.
beta: Parties reach the east end of the Terror Glacier via the same Terror Basin approach as the West Ridge, then climb roughly six pitches of alpine rock (up to 5.8-, rated PG13) up the southwest ridge/face to the summit. There is no pitch-by-pitch description; most parties climb it fully roped rather than scrambled.
